server.description: The physical units, deterministic: a unit as written resolved to its quantity and its UCUM code, a value converted between units of one quantity, two units compared, and a source's value checked against a request's restatement of it in another unit
server.instructions: Never convert a unit in your head: ask units_convert, and check what you copy from a document with units_validate_connection (the document's value and unit as the source, yours as the target). A unit the system does not know is refused, never guessed: write the quantity beside it.

units_normalize.title: Resolve a unit
units_normalize.description: A unit as written (m3/min, m³/min, L/min, ppm, kg/s...), with its quantity when known (VolumetricFlow, Concentration, MassFlow...): the quantity it belongs to, its UCUM code, its symbol and its factor to the quantity's base unit. Ambiguous without the quantity when the same code belongs to two quantities.

units_convert.title: Convert a value
units_convert.description: A value converted from one unit to another of the same quantity, by the substrate's tables; refused across quantities (m3/min to kg/s is not a conversion).

units_compatible.title: Compare two units
units_compatible.description: Whether two units measure the same quantity, and which quantities they measure when they do not.

units_validate_connection.title: Check a restated value
units_validate_connection.description: A source states a value in its unit (a datasheet: 1.0 m3/min); a request restates it in another (60 L/min). Converted, they must agree within the tolerance (2 percent by default): OK with the expected value, or INVALID_CONVERSION with what the restatement should have been.

units_relations.title: The relations between quantities
units_relations.description: The conversions between different quantities a physical relation ties together, each with its formula, its parameters (their units, the cabin's defaults) and which side is a derived reading rather than a quantity of the unit system: a gas's volume flow and mass flow, a fraction in ppm and a mass per volume, a mass flow into a volume and the rate its fraction changes.

units_relate.title: Convert to a related quantity
units_relate.description: A value converted from one quantity to a related one (units_relations lists them), instead of redoing the physics: 0.69 g/min of CO2 as L/min, 1000 ppm as mg/m3, a scrubber's kg/s from a 30 m3 volume as ppm per minute. The answer names the formula and says which parameters were given and which took the cabin's default (101 325 Pa, 293.15 K, CO2's molar mass). Refused when no relation ties the two quantities, or a parameter without a default (a volume) is missing.

properties.value: the value, in the from unit
properties.from: its quantity and unit, e.g. {quantity: MassFlow, unit: g/min}
properties.to: the related quantity and the unit wanted, e.g. {quantity: VolumetricFlow, unit: L/min}
properties.parameters: by name, a number in the parameter's unit or {value, unit}: V (the volume, m3), P (Pa), T (K), M (kg/mol)
